data.name: Mohit
data.gender_notes: Mohit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'mohana' which means 'to intoxicate'. Mohit is a name of Lord Krishna, who intoxicated the gopis with his divine love. The name Mohit carries the meaning “Intoxicated with love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mohit usually hope their child will grow to embody intoxicated with love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name of Lord Krishna, symbolizing intoxication with divine love.
data.etymology: Mohit belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Intoxicated with love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mohit total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mohit is commonly found in Hindu communities, especially in Indian Subcontinent. It can be used as both a given name (first name) and a surname. In popular culture, Mohit is often associated with Lord Krishna, who is known to have enchanted and intoxicated the gopis through his divine love and playfulness. The word "Mohit" can also be used to describe a charismatic and charming person who has the power to captivate others' hearts and minds.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mohit holds deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Sanskrit word 'mohana', which means 'intoxication', 'enchantment', or 'delusion'. It is a name of Lord Krishna, who used his divine love and enchanting personality to intoxicate the gopis, leading them to lose their senses and devote themselves completely to him. Mohit thus represents the power of love and divine grace to transform and uplift the human consciousness, and serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal of all spiritual practices: to attain divine love and union with the ultimate reality.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mohit: Enchanted one, lost in the intoxication of life and love. Often, the playful deity of illusions, leading one away from their spiritual path.
